newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: MEXICO'S CARDENAS URGES DEVELOPMENT DEAL FOR LATAM.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO'S CARDENAS URGES DEVELOPMENT DEAL FOR LATAM.

text.p: Mexican opposition leader and mayor-elect Cuauhtemoc Cardenas said Friday he would prefer a treaty on development with the United States for Latin America rather than a proposed America Free Trade Area.

"We think it would be more convenient (to not follow) this path of setting up a free trade area starting with bilateral agreements between the United States and every one of the Latin American countries," Cardenas told foreign correspondents while on a visit to Argentina.
"We think it would be more convenient to make a proposal for a development treaty for the whole continent," he said.
Cardenas, a twice-failed presidential candidate, leads Mexico's opposition and is the founder of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution.
Cardenas made history on July 6 when he was elected as the first opposition leader of Mexico's capital city in 68 years under the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).

The leaders of the 34 countries in the Americas working toward AFTA are expected to launch formal negotiations for a hemisphere-wide trade agreement early next year in Chile. They hope AFTA will be a reality in 2005.
Cardenas said a treaty for development should be aimed at protecting smallest Latin American economies with subsidies to cushion them against the abrupt liberalization of markets.

The Mexican opposition leader said Latin America should advance along similar lines to the European Union, which used subsidies to help along member-states that were less developed economically, like Spain, Greece and Portugal.
